findings.title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `[z.string().toString()]` as computed keys, evaluating to `"[object Object]"` and stripping expiry fields
findings.body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` invoke `Object.prototype.toString()` on the Zod schema instances, which both evaluate to the literal property name `"[object Object]"`. The second property overwrites the first in the object literal, and because `z.object()` strips unknown keys by default, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` neither validates that a numeric expiry field is present nor preserves any fields other than `access_token` (such as `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, or `instance_url`). Any caller relying on expiry or provider-specific fields in `refreshTokenResponse.data` will receive `undefined`.

findings.title: `GoogleCalendarService` persists the Zod `SafeParseReturnType` wrapper as `credential.key` and assumes `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Gaxios response
findings.body:
There are two bugs in `refreshAccessToken`:
1. `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), whereas previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` returned the parsed credential object directly. Passing `key` to `prisma.credential.update` saves `{ success: true, data: ... }` as `credential.key` in the database, corrupting the credential so that `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 will fail with a `ZodError` on subsequent requests (even when credential sharing is disabled).
2. When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a standard `fetch` `Response` object rather than the `GaxiosResponse` returned by `myGoogleAuth.refreshToken`. `res?.data` on line 94 will be `undefined`, causing `token.access_token` on line 95 to throw a `TypeError`.

findings.title: Missing `prisma` import, missing `refreshOAuthTokens` wrapper, and stale `accessToken` used in `SalesforceCalendarService`
findings.body:
In `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient`:
1. Line 96 calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)`, but `prisma` is not imported in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, causing a TypeScript build failure and a runtime `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined`.
2. Line 75 calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` directly instead of wrapping the request in `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce token refreshes never use `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`.
3. Line 106 passes the stale `credentialKey.access_token` to `new jsforce.Connection(...)` instead of the newly refreshed `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

findings.title: `BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken` passes `credentialId` instead of `userId` and crashes when `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response`
findings.body:
1. Line 93 passes `credentialId` (`credential.id`) as the third argument (`userId`) to `refreshOAuthTokens`, which sends the credential's database ID instead of `credential.userId` as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint.
2. The fallback callback uses `axios.post(...)` (which returns `{ data: ... }`), whereas `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch` `Response` when credential syncing is enabled. On a `fetch` `Response`, `tokenInfo.data` is `undefined`, causing `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` on line 96 to throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`.

findings.title: `ZohoCrmCalendarService` expects an Axios response with `.data`, throwing a `TypeError` when `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response`
findings.body: In `refreshAccessToken`, the callback passed to `refreshOAuthTokens` uses `axios(...)`, which returns an object with a `.data` property, but when credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` object. Accessing `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` on line 217 throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`.

findings.title: `HubspotCalendarService` treats the raw `fetch` `Response` from `refreshOAuthTokens` as a parsed `HubspotToken`
findings.body: `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken` resolves directly to a `TokenResponseIF` object (`{ accessToken, expiresIn, refreshToken, tokenType }`), whereas `refreshOAuthTokens` returns an unparsed `fetch` `Response` when credential syncing is enabled. Consequently, `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` and `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` are `undefined`, `hubspotRefreshToken.expiryDate` evaluates to `NaN`, and `prisma.credential.update` overwrites `credential.key` with the `Response` object.

findings.title: `ZoomVideoApiAdapter` passes `"zoomvideo"` instead of `"zoom"` as `appSlug` to `refreshOAuthTokens`
findings.body: Line 92 passes `"zoomvideo"` as the `appSlug` argument to `refreshOAuthTokens`, whereas the Zoom app's slug in the database and `appStoreMetadata` (and used in `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` and `/api/webhook/app-credential`) is `"zoom"`.

findings.title: `WebexVideoApiAdapter` does not use `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, causing synced token responses to fail schema validation
findings.body: `refreshAccessToken` calls `refreshOAuthTokens`, but line 88 still validates `responseBody` with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)` instead of `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, webexRefreshedTokenSchema)`. Because `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` strictly requires `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`, a minimal response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` containing only the access token and expiry will fail validation.
